newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Bolivia to join booming Mercosur trading bloc.
newsitem.headline: Bolivia to join booming Mercosur trading bloc.

text.p: The presidents of Latin America's Mercosur trading bloc were arriving here Monday for their annual summit, the highlight of which will be the signing of a free trade agreement with neighboring Bolivia.

The announcement of the long-awaited Bolivian free trade agreement, scheduled for Tuesday, was almost canceled Sunday by a last minute dispute over wheat and wheat flour exports between Bolivia and Argentina.
"We will benefit by winning access to an economy like that of Brazil and by being forced to compete with their products," he said.

Other items on the summit agenda are a plan to establish Mercosur's administrative headquarters in Montevideo and a proposal under which the Mercosur partners will recognize the social security commitments of citizens of member countries.

The presidents are also expected to approve a Mercosur logo, which will show the four stars of the Southern Cross, and which they hope will become recognized as a brand of quality for the trade bloc's products around the world.
Negotiators had hoped but failed to agree on a common Defense of Competition which would define and regulate dumping within Mercosur borders.

Brazil and Argentina have also disagreed on the implementation of a document defining a common safeguard policy which would allow Mercosur partners to take action in case of dumping by a country outside the trade group.
